realWorldScenario.title: The quiet printer is missing from a switch table
realWorldScenario.takeaway: A dynamic table is a recent forwarding aid, not an inventory database. Combine traffic, VLAN and interface observations before concluding that an absent record represents failed equipment.
realWorldScenario.situation: In a hypothetical small office, an operator cannot find a printer's MAC in a current table snapshot and proposes rebooting the switch. The printer has been idle, and its physical port is still up. A missing learned record may reflect normal aging. The useful question is what arrives when the printer sends traffic, not whether the table remembers it forever.
walkthrough: Record the VLAN, port status, table timestamp and printer's actual interface MAC before changing anything.
Generate an authorized small test to the printer, understanding that a response creates source-learning evidence.
Compare the endpoint's ARP mapping with the switch's separate VLAN-to-MAC-to-port relationship.
If the expected source is still absent, inspect port membership and ingress evidence rather than clearing unrelated tables.
Record the limited result: local delivery was observed or remains unresolved; do not infer printer application health from ping.

glossary.meaning: A virtual LAN is a logical Layer 2 group. Broadcast frames remain within that group's eligible forwarding ports. A VLAN does not encrypt traffic or automatically provide a route to another VLAN.
An access port normally places untagged data frames into one configured data VLAN. A voice VLAN is a special additional edge-port capability, not permission for an arbitrary set of tagged VLANs.
VLAN 1 is the default Ethernet VLAN. Normal-range IDs are 1 through 1005; IDs 1002 through 1005 are legacy reserved defaults. Use ordinary lab IDs 10, 20 and 30 rather than deleting defaults.

A voice VLAN separates a phone's voice frames from its attached computer's data frames. An 802.1Q tag carries VLAN information; a compatible phone can tag voice while passing untagged computer traffic.

Power over Ethernet delivers electrical power on supported cabling. The power sourcing equipment is the switch or injector; the powered device is the phone or AP. VLAN configuration does not create electrical power.

An access point joins wireless clients to a wired network. A virtualized host runs multiple virtual machines. Their uplinks can need one untagged network or several tagged networks depending on design.
A subnet is an IP prefix group. A gateway routes packets between IP networks. Putting two same-prefix endpoints in different VLANs does not supply the missing local delivery path.

The Console is the named device's management window. Verification compares intended configuration with operational state and a specific traffic test; a displayed configuration alone does not prove service.

sections.example: H1 and H2 keep their /24 addresses during the fault. H1 still regards H2 as local, but its local discovery cannot reach H2's new VLAN. Changing H1's mask would change a second variable rather than repair the misplaced port.
sections.heading: VLAN membership is independent of the IP prefix
keyPoints: Create and verify the intended group before testing traffic.
A link-up indication does not prove correct VLAN membership.
sections.explanation: A switch groups Layer 2 ports without deriving the group from the address inside each packet. Hosts commonly share one IP subnet per VLAN, but those two concepts remain distinct. Moving a port does not rewrite its host's address. VLAN separation limits local forwarding; it supplies neither encryption nor a router.

sections.example: Read show vlan brief on a fresh switch before changing it. Seeing VLAN 1 does not mean it must be used for users or management. Never delete default records or erase vlan.dat to force the display to resemble a classroom screenshot.
sections.heading: Know the defaults without depending on them
keyPoints: VLAN ID and VLAN name are different fields; a name is not an address.
The current v1.1 normal-range objective is only partially completed here; multi-switch and routed use follow.
sections.explanation: VLAN 1 is the default Ethernet VLAN and default access membership on these IOS switch platforms. The normal range is 1-1005, with 1002-1005 reserved for legacy defaults. Ordinary configurable Ethernet lab VLANs such as 10 and 20 are inside that range. Extended IDs 1006-4094 are a separate range, not needed here.

sections.example: In this exercise Gi0/2 is reserved, unplugged and shut down. Setting data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30 there lets the learner inspect both fields safely. Without a phone, no tagged voice traffic, phone registration or call quality is observed.
sections.heading: A phone edge can carry data and voice separately
keyPoints: Verify the voice VLAN exists and read the interface's switchport details.
A phone's attached computer should not be assumed to share the voice subnet.
sections.explanation: With a compatible phone, the access VLAN carries ordinary untagged computer data and the configured voice VLAN carries tagged voice traffic. Discovery and endpoint configuration must agree. This specialized access-port behavior should not be described as an unrestricted trunk. A voice VLAN is also not a complete QoS policy or call-control configuration.

sections.example: Before deploying an AP port, document whether clients are locally bridged, the management VLAN and which side tags each network. For a hypervisor, confirm its virtual-switch VLAN and aggregation mode with the host owner. Day 18 teaches trunks and Day 22 handles LACP rather than guessing here.
sections.heading: Choose edge attributes from the actual endpoint design
keyPoints: Never configure all AP or server ports identically without checking their design.
This chapter provides a selection framework, not tested AP or hypervisor service.
sections.explanation: A desktop, printer or simple appliance often needs one data access VLAN. A standalone AP advertising several locally bridged networks may require a trunk; a controller-based AP can use an access management VLAN when its traffic is centrally tunneled. A virtualized host can need tagged VLANs or an explicitly configured link aggregation group. None of those requirements follows from a label alone.

sections.example: Optional physical observation: on an authorized spare Catalyst 2960-X PoE switch with IOS 15.2(7)E and a compatible phone, open its local serial Console and run show power inline. Compare admin/oper state, allocation and remaining budget. Do not modify power limits or attach unknown injectors; no such hardware was used here.
sections.heading: Power delivery is a separate physical dependency
keyPoints: Treat unsupported virtual power commands as a platform boundary, not a reason to invent wattage.
Do not override consumption budgets to make a device power on.
sections.explanation: PoE requires a compatible powered device, a capable sourcing port, suitable cabling and adequate available budget. Virtual IOSvL2 does not generate electrical watts. A configured voice VLAN cannot fix denied power, and a powered phone can still have incorrect VLAN settings. Keep power and data evidence in separate worksheet columns.

sections.example: v1.1 2.1.a-b and 1.1.h receive direct teaching here with bounded data/voice configuration and conceptual PoE. v2.0 2.2 receives partial edge-port coverage. LACP, full AP service and virtual-host integration remain later or equipment-dependent work.
sections.heading: Restore one attribute and repeat the same test
keyPoints: Do not save a deliberate fault into the desired baseline.
Preserve observed output and label all unexecuted exercises as predictions.
sections.explanation: A wrong-access-VLAN fault can leave the interface up and the IP address unchanged. Read the port's administrative mode, operational mode and access VLAN, then compare with the known working state. Restore only the intended membership. A successful retest supports that selected local path, not every VLAN or application.

content.plainAnswer: A VLAN defines a separate Layer 2 broadcast domain. An access port assigns ordinary untagged endpoint traffic to its data VLAN; a compatible phone can additionally use a configured voice VLAN. Create the VLAN, set the edge-port mode and membership, then verify both the switch state and the intended peer test. Matching IP prefixes do not overcome different VLAN membership.

firstPractice.hint: The local ARP request is an Ethernet broadcast and remains in its VLAN; an IP mask does not select a switch's access VLAN.
firstPractice.task: On paper, give two endpoints 192.0.2.10/24 and 192.0.2.20/24 but place their access ports in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. Predict whether ordinary local ARP can reach the other endpoint without routing or bridging between groups.
firstPractice.expected: It cannot cross the separate VLAN boundary merely because the IPv4 prefixes match.

beginnerGuide.startingPoint: Imagine the switch's ports sorted into labeled groups. Draw Gi0/0 and Gi0/1 inside VLAN 10, then draw an empty VLAN 20 group. The upcoming fault moves only Gi0/1 between those groups.

checkUnderstanding.hint: List what is absent from a port's configuration display.
checkUnderstanding.answer: No. It establishes a port attribute only. A compatible powered phone, discovery or provisioning, addressing and the voice service path must also work; no call is tested in this virtual lab.
checkUnderstanding.question: Does configuring voice VLAN 30 prove that a phone can make calls?

everydayComparison.whereItStops: VLANs are forwarding boundaries, not acoustic walls or encryption. Their isolation depends on correct configuration and other security controls.
everydayComparison.networkMeaning: The chassis is the building and the VLAN groups are rooms. Port membership determines the local conversation; routing is a separately provided path between groups.
everydayComparison.familiarSituation: A building can contain several separate meeting rooms even when every participant uses the same street address. Being in the building does not put everyone in the same conversation.

content.learnerOutcome: Create normal-range VLANs, identify the default VLAN, inspect data and voice edge-port attributes, repair a single wrong-access-VLAN fault, and explain which AP, virtual-host and PoE checks require additional equipment.
content.metaDescription: Build and repair access VLAN membership, verify data and voice settings, and distinguish virtual switching evidence from real PoE and endpoint behavior.

terms.meaning: A virtual LAN is a logical Layer 2 group. Broadcast frames remain within that group's eligible forwarding ports. A VLAN does not encrypt traffic or automatically provide a route to another VLAN.
An access port normally places untagged data frames into one configured data VLAN. A voice VLAN is a special additional edge-port capability, not permission for an arbitrary set of tagged VLANs.
VLAN 1 is the default Ethernet VLAN. Normal-range IDs are 1 through 1005; IDs 1002 through 1005 are legacy reserved defaults. Use ordinary lab IDs 10, 20 and 30 rather than deleting defaults.

A voice VLAN separates a phone's voice frames from its attached computer's data frames. An 802.1Q tag carries VLAN information; a compatible phone can tag voice while passing untagged computer traffic.

Power over Ethernet delivers electrical power on supported cabling. The power sourcing equipment is the switch or injector; the powered device is the phone or AP. VLAN configuration does not create electrical power.

An access point joins wireless clients to a wired network. A virtualized host runs multiple virtual machines. Their uplinks can need one untagged network or several tagged networks depending on design.
A subnet is an IP prefix group. A gateway routes packets between IP networks. Putting two same-prefix endpoints in different VLANs does not supply the missing local delivery path.

The Console is the named device's management window. Verification compares intended configuration with operational state and a specific traffic test; a displayed configuration alone does not prove service.

teachingPrelude.explanation: Start with membership, not an IP address guess. Two sockets on the same chassis can belong to different local networks. We first prove a common-VLAN path, then move one port into an unused VLAN and use switch evidence to explain the failure.
teachingPrelude.labBoundary: One virtual switch and two IOSv test endpoints form the executable lab. No phone, AP, hypervisor or powered device is attached. Voice configuration is inspected only; PoE and those endpoint services remain practical alternatives.

practiceQuestions.answer: Their ports can belong to different VLANs.
practiceQuestions.question: Why can two /24 peers still fail on one switch?
practiceQuestions.explanation: An IP prefix does not move Ethernet broadcasts across separate Layer 2 domains; inspect the access membership.

practiceQuestions.answer: VLAN 1 is the default on the documented IOS platforms.
practiceQuestions.question: Which VLAN is the default Ethernet VLAN?
practiceQuestions.explanation: A default value is not a design mandate; the lab explicitly uses VLAN 10 and does not delete default records.

practiceQuestions.answer: No; 1002-1005 are reserved legacy defaults.
practiceQuestions.question: Are all IDs 1-1005 ordinary user VLANs?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Normal-range terminology includes these IDs, but the lesson uses ordinary configurable Ethernet VLANs such as 10.

practiceQuestions.answer: The access data VLAN and configured voice VLAN attributes.
practiceQuestions.question: What separates phone data from voice here?
practiceQuestions.explanation: A compatible phone must handle the expected tagging; an access voice feature is not an arbitrary multi-VLAN trunk.

practiceQuestions.answer: No; it does not deliver electrical power.

practiceQuestions.explanation: Physical port capability, powered-device requirements and budget need real authorized hardware observations.

practiceQuestions.answer: Only access membership is the intended changed variable.
practiceQuestions.question: Why not change H2's address during the fault?

realWorldScenario.title: The moved desk has link but cannot reach its neighbor
realWorldScenario.takeaway: Physical connectivity, VLAN membership and IP configuration are separate facts. Restoring the intended port attribute is more defensible than repeatedly changing an otherwise correct address.
realWorldScenario.situation: A hypothetical desk move reconnects a computer to a spare port assigned to a different department. Its static IPv4 address is unchanged and its link is up, so the user blames the address plan. The operator has a prior port worksheet and can compare intended membership before changing the host.

glossary.meaning: An Ethernet trunk carries multiple VLANs over one physical or logical link. It keeps those Layer 2 domains distinct; it does not route between them.
An 802.1Q tag adds VLAN information to an Ethernet frame on a trunk. The VLAN identifier is not an IP address and does not encrypt the frame.

On this default untagged-native IOS configuration, an untagged frame received on a trunk is associated with that port's native VLAN. Native IDs must agree at both ends; native tagging options change behavior and are outside this lab.
This list restricts which VLANs may traverse a trunk. A VLAN must also exist and be active and have a forwarding path; appearing in the allowed list alone does not prove delivery.

Dynamic Trunking Protocol can negotiate trunking between compatible Cisco interfaces. Explicit trunk mode with nonegotiate avoids depending on that negotiation; both peers must be configured deliberately.
A switched virtual interface is the switch's logical IP attachment to one VLAN. Here VLAN 20 SVIs are same-subnet test endpoints, not inter-VLAN routers.
Spanning Tree Protocol controls Layer 2 forwarding to prevent loops. Even an allowed, active VLAN can have a non-forwarding port because of spanning-tree state.
Console gives direct management access to the selected virtual node. A baseline records operational trunk state and successful tests in each used VLAN before any allowed-list change.

sections.example: H1 sends untagged data into SW1 Gi0/0, which classifies it as VLAN 10. SW1's trunk sends it with VLAN 10 tagging because 10 is not native. SW2 receives it in VLAN 10 and delivers untagged data through H2's access port.
sections.heading: Tagging preserves separate local networks
keyPoints: The complete data path ends at H2, not at the second switch.
VLAN tags provide separation context, not confidentiality.
sections.explanation: A tag provides VLAN identity on a shared Ethernet link so the receiving switch can keep traffic in the intended local domain. Access-facing endpoint frames normally need no tag because the access port supplies membership. The switch adds or removes tagging as appropriate at the boundary; it does not route simply by changing the Ethernet representation.

sections.example: Use unused VLAN 999 at both trunk endpoints, with no user access ports assigned to it. This reduces ambiguity in the lesson but is not a complete security design. A mismatch can cause incorrect classification and spanning-tree protection symptoms; it does not imply every tagged VLAN must fail.
sections.heading: Native means a shared classification convention
keyPoints: Compare native values on both sides rather than reading one configuration.
Do not induce a native mismatch on a shared or production link.
sections.explanation: Under the lab's default untagged-native behavior, native-VLAN frames leave untagged and received untagged frames enter the local native VLAN. Both sides therefore need the same native ID. Some platforms can tag native traffic explicitly; that is a separate setting and must not be silently assumed. Native VLAN and default access VLAN are distinct attributes.

sections.example: When VLAN 10 is removed only on SW2, SW1's allowed list can still look correct. The end-to-end path is nevertheless broken. Adding VLAN 10 back is targeted recovery; replacing the full list carelessly could remove VLAN 20 at the same time.
sections.heading: Allowed is only one of several gates
keyPoints: Use add/remove when making a deliberate incremental change to an existing list.
A bare allowed-vlan list sets the list rather than appending to it.
sections.explanation: The allowed list is a configured permission. VLAN existence and active state are separate, and spanning-tree state determines forwarding eligibility. IOS trunk output exposes these distinctions in separate lists. A VLAN may be allowed but absent, or active but not forwarding. Read the full output and correlate it with the selected port.

sections.example: IOSvL2 supports an encapsulation selector, while a fixed-802.1Q switch may reject that command because there is no choice to select. That difference is a platform issue, not proof that the device cannot trunk. Record the exact image and use its documentation.
sections.heading: Choose explicit peer behavior
keyPoints: Administrative mode and operational mode are not interchangeable evidence.
Stop on rejected syntax rather than pasting the rest of the block blindly.
sections.explanation: DTP negotiation is not necessary for a manually configured trunk. Two passive dynamic-auto peers do not actively initiate trunk formation. A router or another vendor's endpoint may not implement DTP at all. This lab explicitly configures each peer and suppresses negotiation, which makes the intended state easy to compare.

sections.example: v1.1 2.2 and the multi-switch portion of 2.1 are directly practiced. Announced v2.0 2.1.b is the primary trunk mapping; 2.4 receives partial diagnostic practice. Inter-VLAN routing and LACP remain separate lessons.
sections.heading: Keep the diagnosis VLAN-specific
keyPoints: Record actual before/fault/after output; no author runtime is claimed.
A successful same-VLAN test does not establish routing between VLAN 10 and 20.
sections.explanation: The lab has a data test and a control test, not two different routes around the fault. VLAN 20 traverses the same physical cable but is independently allowed. This makes a useful comparison: a physical failure would affect both, while the intended allowed-list fault affects VLAN 10. Other real faults can still have selective symptoms, so the observed configuration is essential.

content.metaTitle: CCNA Day 18: 802.1Q Trunks and Native VLANs
takeaways: A trunk extends VLANs without routing between them.
Native VLAN classification must agree at both ends.
Allowed, active and forwarding are distinct checks.
A link can stay up while one VLAN is unavailable.
Use an incremental list change when preserving existing members.
Test the affected VLAN and an independent control before closing recovery.
objectives: Explain tagged and untagged-native frame classification.
Configure matching trunk mode, native VLAN and allowed lists.
Distinguish allowed, active and forwarding evidence.
Repair a missing allowed VLAN without disabling unrelated traffic.
Predict a native mismatch and state the limits of a single successful ping.
content.plainAnswer: An 802.1Q trunk carries separate VLANs over a shared link. Most data VLAN frames are tagged; in this lab the native VLAN uses untagged carriage. Verify both ends' operational mode, native VLAN and allowed/active/forwarding VLAN lists. A physical link can remain up while one VLAN is missing. Trunking extends Layer 2 domains; routing between them is a separate function.

visualStory.title: A trunk has more than one gate

stages.title: Read allowed membership
stages.explanation: VLAN 10 must be allowed on both trunk endpoints. Removing it on one side breaks the selected path.

stages.explanation: An allowed number is not proof of an active VLAN database entry. Check both switches.

beginnerGuide.whyItMatters: A trunk fault can affect only one department even while other traffic crosses the same cable. Keeping physical state separate from VLAN-specific evidence narrows the investigation quickly.

firstPractice.hint: An untagged frame does not carry the sender's native VLAN number; the receiving port supplies its local classification.
firstPractice.task: On paper, set the native VLAN to 999 on SW1 and 20 on SW2. Trace an untagged frame sent on that cable and state which VLAN SW2 associates with its reception. Do not implement this mismatch in a connected network.
firstPractice.expected: SW2 associates the untagged arrival with its native VLAN 20, not SW1's intended 999.

beginnerGuide.startingPoint: Draw two switches joined by one cable, then write VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 beside that cable as separate logical memberships. Place H1 and H2 in VLAN 10 and two switch test addresses in VLAN 20.

checkUnderstanding.hint: Ask which source and destination the successful test actually used.
checkUnderstanding.answer: No. The result covers the VLAN 20 path only. Check VLAN 10 existence, allowed membership and forwarding state on both ends, then test its own endpoints.
checkUnderstanding.question: The trunk is up and VLAN 20 pings work. Is VLAN 10 verified?

everydayComparison.whereItStops: A trunk is not a router or a delivery scheduler. Native untagged classification and spanning-tree forwarding rules have no exact vehicle equivalent.
everydayComparison.networkMeaning: The road represents the physical link, the labels represent VLAN tags and the permitted consignments represent the allowed list. Each destination must interpret labels consistently.
everydayComparison.familiarSituation: A delivery vehicle carries several separately labeled consignments on one road. The road being open says nothing about whether a particular consignment was permitted onto the vehicle.

On this default untagged-native IOS configuration, an untagged frame received on a trunk is associated with that port's native VLAN. Native IDs must agree at both ends; native tagging options change behavior and are outside this lab.
This list restricts which VLANs may traverse a trunk. A VLAN must also exist and be active and have a forwarding path; appearing in the allowed list alone does not prove delivery.

Dynamic Trunking Protocol can negotiate trunking between compatible Cisco interfaces. Explicit trunk mode with nonegotiate avoids depending on that negotiation; both peers must be configured deliberately.
A switched virtual interface is the switch's logical IP attachment to one VLAN. Here VLAN 20 SVIs are same-subnet test endpoints, not inter-VLAN routers.
Spanning Tree Protocol controls Layer 2 forwarding to prevent loops. Even an allowed, active VLAN can have a non-forwarding port because of spanning-tree state.
Console gives direct management access to the selected virtual node. A baseline records operational trunk state and successful tests in each used VLAN before any allowed-list change.

glossary.meaning: Routing moves an IP packet between different networks, including networks attached to separate VLANs. A trunk alone carries VLAN frames but does not make that routing decision.
One router Ethernet interface uses several logical subinterfaces, each associated with a VLAN. The shared cable carries traffic toward the router and back toward the destination VLAN.
A subinterface is a logical subdivision of a physical parent interface, such as Gi0/0.10. The suffix is a local label; encapsulation dot1q 10, not the suffix itself, selects VLAN 10.

A gateway is the next-hop router for an off-subnet destination. Our IOSv test endpoints use an explicit default route to mimic that host choice; their command syntax differs from a desktop gateway setting.
A connected route describes a network attached to an operational IP interface. R1 can route between its two connected /24 networks without a static route for either one.
ARP discovers a local next-hop MAC for IPv4. The router removes the incoming frame and builds a new outgoing frame; the end-to-end IP destination remains H2 in this no-NAT lab.
The native VLAN classifies untagged traffic under this lab's default behavior. VLAN 999 matches at both trunk ends and has no user IP address; VLANs 10 and 20 are tagged.
Console provides direct access independent of the data cable. Rollback restores the exact known change, here a single subinterface shutdown, before repeating the original traffic test.

sections.example: R1 Gi0/0.10 uses encapsulation dot1q 10. Its .10 suffix makes the configuration readable, but changing only the suffix would not change the VLAN. A mistaken encapsulation dot1q 30 would listen in the wrong logical domain even with the desired IP address.
sections.heading: Make one physical connection serve two gateways
keyPoints: Keep the parent enabled and verify its cable state.
Do not place overlapping subnets on different gateway subinterfaces.
sections.explanation: The router parent provides the physical connection. Logical subinterfaces provide VLAN-specific IP attachments. In this design the parent has no IP address, VLAN 10 uses 192.0.2.1/24 and VLAN 20 uses 198.51.100.1/24. Each prefix is different and each endpoint has the corresponding local gateway.

sections.example: Without NAT, H1's source IP and H2's destination IP remain end-to-end, while Ethernet addresses change at the router. IPv4 TTL decreases during routing and the header checksum changes accordingly. A trunk tag is not an IP route and does not authorize application access.
sections.heading: Trace the complete request and reply
keyPoints: The physical router cable carries both arrival and departure traffic.
A reply needs H2's correct local gateway as well as H1's.
sections.explanation: H1 sends an off-subnet packet inside a frame addressed to its local gateway. SW1 carries the VLAN 10 frame to R1. R1 makes an IP routing decision, then builds a new VLAN 20 frame toward H2. SW1 delivers that through H2's access port. The return takes the corresponding reverse routing decisions.

sections.example: If SW1 permits only VLAN 10, R1's VLAN 20 interface configuration alone cannot make H2 reachable. Likewise, a correct allowed list cannot fix an encapsulation ID that maps the router gateway into a different VLAN. Compare both configuration and actual test evidence.
sections.heading: A router trunk is deliberately configured
keyPoints: An up/up subinterface is not proof that the remote VLAN is carried correctly.
Native VLAN 999 has no endpoint or IP service in this experiment.
sections.explanation: The switch must carry both data VLANs and agree with the router on any native classification. R1 does not rely on DTP to create its subinterfaces. This lab uses explicit trunk mode and no negotiation on SW1, with unused native VLAN 999 matched by an unaddressed native subinterface.

sections.example: After shutting R1 Gi0/0.20, expect its connected network route to disappear while VLAN 10 remains operational. H1 should still reach 192.0.2.1 but not H2. This controlled contrast differs from a tag mismatch, which may leave an interface appearing up.
sections.heading: Use connected-route evidence carefully
keyPoints: No static route is needed on R1 for either directly connected subnet.
Endpoint IOSv default routes are included because these test nodes otherwise lack an off-subnet path.
sections.explanation: A connected route indicates R1's local network attachment is operational from its perspective. It does not prove that every host in that prefix is reachable or that the switch trunk is correctly carrying the VLAN. Use show ip interface brief, the interface configuration and show ip route together with gateway and peer tests.

sections.example: For v1.1 this contributes to 2.1.c inter-VLAN connectivity and 2.2 trunk skills. For announced v2.0 it supports 2.1 infrastructure connectivity, with direct trunk practice and partial Layer 3 diagnostics. It is not SVI configuration; that is Day 20.
sections.heading: Know what the model does not establish
keyPoints: No gateway redundancy or security policy is configured here.
Only actually executed results can be reported as observations.
sections.explanation: One shared cable is a dependency for both gateways. Its capacity and hardware forwarding behavior depend on real equipment, while CML virtual images have performance limitations. Do not use this exercise to quote production throughput, convergence time or firewall effectiveness. Routing also permits traffic unless additional policy constrains it.

content.metaTitle: CCNA Day 19: Router-on-a-Stick Inter-VLAN Routing
takeaways: A router subinterface provides a VLAN-specific Layer 3 attachment.
The encapsulation VLAN ID matters more than the suffix convention.
The same trunk cable carries ingress and egress VLAN contexts.
Connected routes do not replace endpoint tests.
Return gateway configuration is part of successful connectivity.
Selective failure evidence should lead to a selective restoration.
objectives: Map each VLAN to its router subinterface and unique IP subnet.
Distinguish a subinterface suffix from its encapsulation VLAN ID.
Configure the parent link, gateways and endpoint return paths.
Correlate interface state with connected routes and peer tests.
Disable and restore only one isolated subinterface without claiming hardware performance.
content.plainAnswer: Router-on-a-stick uses one physical router link with a logical subinterface per VLAN. Each subinterface needs the correct 802.1Q VLAN mapping and an IP address in that VLAN's subnet. Hosts use their local router address for other networks. Verify access VLANs, trunk carriage, subinterface state, connected routes and both directions of the endpoint exchange.

glossary.meaning: A switchport forwards Ethernet frames within VLANs. An access port belongs to one ordinary data VLAN; an 802.1Q trunk can carry multiple VLANs.
A switched virtual interface gives a switch a logical IP attachment to one VLAN. On a routing-capable switch it can be that VLAN's gateway; merely creating it does not enable transit routing.
A physical interface configured with no switchport becomes a Layer 3 port with an IP address on the port itself. It is not an access member or a trunk for the old VLAN.
IP routing enables packet forwarding between IP interfaces on a capable switch. A management-only default gateway setting is not a replacement for routing configuration.

Normal SVI operational state depends on an active VLAN, an enabled SVI and at least one eligible up Layer 2 member in forwarding state. Platform exceptions exist; this lesson uses the normal IOSvL2 model.
An operational addressed IP interface supplies a connected network route. The route can disappear when the interface's protocol goes down even though the address remains in configuration.
Syslog records device events. A message has a facility, severity and mnemonic plus descriptive content. A recorded state transition is evidence of an event, not automatic proof of its root cause.
Console is direct management of the named node. A control test follows an unaffected path during the fault, helping distinguish selective VLAN failure from complete device failure.

sections.example: SW1 Gi0/0 is access VLAN 10 with no IP address. Vlan10 has 192.0.2.1/24. Gi0/2 uses no switchport and 203.0.113.1/30 toward R2. Putting an address on Gi0/0 by converting it would change the design rather than configure the VLAN 10 gateway.
sections.heading: Three interface types serve different purposes
keyPoints: Check show interfaces switchport to distinguish Layer 2 from routed behavior.
Do not run no switchport on an existing user trunk or shared access port.
sections.explanation: A Layer 2 access port associates endpoint frames with a VLAN. An SVI is the switch's logical IP attachment to that VLAN. A routed physical port removes switchport behavior and places an IP network directly on the physical interface. These can coexist on a routing-capable switch without making them interchangeable.

sections.example: H1 at 192.0.2.10 uses 192.0.2.1. H2 at 198.51.100.20 uses 198.51.100.1. A successful exchange crosses the routing function inside SW1, unlike Day 19's external-router trunk. No access policy is configured, so segmentation must not be described as a firewall.
sections.heading: Enable routing but preserve VLAN boundaries
keyPoints: A management default gateway command is not a substitute for transit IP routing.
No static route is needed between these two directly connected operational SVIs.
sections.explanation: With operational SVIs and IP routing enabled, the switch can route packets between the attached prefixes. Endpoints use their local SVI as the next hop for off-subnet destinations. The VLANs remain separate Layer 2 broadcast domains even though an authorized routed path now exists between them.

sections.example: VLAN 20 has only SW1 Gi0/1 in this lab, with no trunk carrying it. Shutting that member should remove Vlan20's operational attachment and its connected route. In a larger network, another forwarding access or trunk member could keep the SVI up.
sections.heading: An SVI has Layer 2 dependencies
keyPoints: Record both status and protocol columns; exact down wording can vary by platform.
Wait for forwarding convergence before concluding an enabled port did not restore the SVI.
sections.explanation: Normal autostate considers VLAN existence and active state, administrative enablement and at least one eligible up forwarding Layer 2 member. The SVI's configured address can remain when those prerequisites fail. Do not defeat this dependency to make a status display look healthy; investigate the real member path.

sections.example: SW1 can ping R2 at 203.0.113.2 using the directly connected link. H1-to-R2 would need a correctly planned return route on R2 and is outside this experiment. Do not report upstream reachability merely because SW1's adjacent peer answers.
sections.heading: A routed uplink is not another VLAN trunk
keyPoints: The routed cable has its own subnet and no access VLAN assignment.
A local link test cannot establish a remote routing service.
sections.explanation: Gi0/2 uses a /30 network directly toward R2. It does not carry VLAN 10 or 20 tags and does not count as a Layer 2 member keeping their SVIs up. Its successful peer ping provides a control during the VLAN 20 fault, but the lab deliberately does not provide R2 with routes to the user VLANs.

sections.example: Illustrative mnemonic LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN means a line-protocol notification with severity 5; it is not an observed lab log. In the experiment, compare Gi0/1's deliberate shutdown time with any Vlan20 transition, then verify traffic. Message ordering and emission can vary by image.
sections.heading: Correlate events, state and traffic
keyPoints: Never invent exact timestamps, message counts or recovery durations.
This covers relevant logs for v2.0 2.4; comprehensive syslog treatment belongs later.
sections.explanation: Read show logging together with interface state and connected routes. A LINK or LINEPROTO event can identify an interface transition, but it does not prove which person, cable or policy caused it. Preserve exact messages if present, including timestamps and clock uncertainty. An empty buffer is not proof that no transition happened.

content.plainAnswer: An SVI is a VLAN's logical IP interface; a routed physical port has its IP address directly on the port. A capable switch with IP routing enabled can forward between these interfaces. An SVI also needs a working Layer 2 VLAN attachment: its address can remain configured while its operational state and connected route disappear.

everydayComparison.networkMeaning: The shared reception resembles an SVI attached to a VLAN's member ports. The dedicated entrance resembles a routed physical port with its own subnet.
everydayComparison.familiarSituation: A department can have a shared reception point used by many doors, while another service has a dedicated entrance. Closing the last department door makes its reception unreachable from that department.

realWorldScenario.title: The gateway address exists, but the gateway is not operational
realWorldScenario.takeaway: Configuration intent, operational attachment and usable traffic are separate claims. The most useful repair restores the dependency that failed, then proves the intended path.
realWorldScenario.situation: A hypothetical administrator sees Vlan20's address in running configuration and assumes the gateway must work. The VLAN's last active access cable was disconnected. Re-entering the same IP address changes no missing dependency and can distract from the actual interface evidence.

lab.title: A missing LLDP advertisement on an intact three-switch chain
cleanup: Restore SW3 Gi0/0 LLDP transmit and retain final protocol and ping evidence.
Stop the isolated nodes after preserving the private corrected worksheet. Do not expose advertised management details or export bundled Cisco images.
devices: SW1: CML 2.10 bundled IOSvL2, IOS 15.2 family; verify exact build and LLDP support.
SW2 and SW3: two matching bundled IOSvL2 nodes, with independent Console access.
lab.topology: SW1 Gi0/0 -- SW2 Gi0/0; SW2 Gi0/1 -- SW3 Gi0/0. All mapped links are access VLAN 10. There is no SW1--SW3 cable, no loop and no external connector.
verification: Record reciprocal cable endpoints rather than a single device name.
Verify global and per-interface protocol state and LLDP directions.
Distinguish direct neighbor scope from the multi-switch ping path.
Wait for actual record expiry after disabling transmit; timing is not assumed.
Confirm restored LLDP visibility and correct only the proven documentation discrepancy.
lab.licensingNote: Use an existing Cisco Modeling Labs 2.10 entitlement and its bundled reference images inside CML only. GNS3 does not provide Cisco images; use images there only when a separate applicable license permits that environment. Do not share or redistribute image files. A CML subscription alone does not authorize exporting its Cisco images to GNS3. Without entitlement, use the explicitly labeled paper exercises; they do not establish hands-on competence.
troubleshooting: If neither protocol finds a peer, check the actual cable and interface state, then global and interface discovery settings on both ends.
If only one protocol is absent, check its support and configuration without assuming an IP failure. Optional advertised fields may legitimately be missing.
If an old entry remains, inspect holdtime/TTL and wait. A cached record does not prove the peer is still sending.
If local and remote port labels conflict, obtain reciprocal evidence and the actual CML cable map before modifying either the network or its records.

glossary.meaning: Cisco Discovery Protocol is a Layer 2 neighbor-discovery protocol. It advertises device and interface information to adjacent compatible devices; it is not a route lookup or an authentication system.
Link Layer Discovery Protocol is a standards-based Layer 2 discovery protocol. Devices advertise information such as chassis ID, port ID and system name through locally scoped messages.

glossary.term: Local interface and remote port ID
glossary.meaning: The local interface is the receiving device's port. The remote port ID is the neighbor's advertised port identifier. Reversing them produces an incorrect cable record.
A chassis ID identifies an advertised device in LLDP; a system name is a human-readable advertised name. Formats differ by platform, and neither is cryptographic proof of identity.
A type-length-value field describes what an advertised item means and how much data it contains. Not every neighbor sends every optional field, such as a management address.
Discovery records expire if advertisements stop. CDP calls its lifetime holdtime; LLDP uses a time-to-live field. A cached record can therefore outlive a recent configuration change.
LLDP transmission sends local advertisements, while reception accepts a neighbor's advertisements. Disabling one direction can create asymmetric neighbor views without breaking ordinary IP traffic.
Console is direct access to the selected lab node. A useful evidence record includes device, local port, remote identity/port, protocol, timestamp and unresolved discrepancies.

sections.example: SW1 should identify SW2, not SW3, in this direct-link topology. SW2 can identify both. All three can still share a VLAN 10 subnet. This contrast explains why Layer 2 data reachability and discovery adjacency are related but different relationships.
sections.heading: Discovery is local evidence, not a network map by itself
keyPoints: Collect both ends rather than treating one table as global truth.
Never use an advertised management address as authorization to log in.
sections.explanation: CDP and LLDP advertise adjacent-device details at Layer 2. To build a wider topology, collect local observations from multiple devices and join matching endpoints. One table is not a substitute for recursively validated documentation, and a management address in an advertisement is not necessarily reachable from the observing host.

sections.example: On SW2, local Gi0/1 and remote Gi0/0 form the SW2-to-SW3 cable record. On SW3, the roles reverse. A port description is operator-entered intent; it can disagree with current discovery and must not automatically override observed cable evidence.
sections.heading: Preserve the direction of the fields
keyPoints: A hostname and a CML canvas label are separate settings until configured.
An absent optional management-address field is not proof that discovery failed.
sections.explanation: Record the observing device and local interface first, then advertised neighbor identity and remote port ID. Include the protocol and timestamp so conflicting snapshots can be reconciled. CDP and LLDP may use different identity formats, so compare meaningful values rather than expecting every string to match byte-for-byte.

sections.example: The lab disables only LLDP transmit on SW3 Gi0/0. SW2 should eventually lose SW3's LLDP advertisement, while SW3 can still receive SW2's advertisements. CDP is left enabled. No buffer clear is needed, and no precise expiry measurement is supplied by the author.
sections.heading: Protocol configuration and aging explain gaps
keyPoints: Do not lower timers on a shared network to make an experiment faster.
If the image lacks LLDP, label that practical branch unsupported rather than replacing it with imagined output.
sections.explanation: CDP has global and interface controls. LLDP also distinguishes transmission from reception. Neighbor records have advertised lifetimes, so a change may not immediately remove a cached entry. Read actual timer or holdtime values and wait for expiry rather than asserting a universal exact delay.

sections.example: Start with a deliberately wrong paper label saying SW2 Gi0/2 connects to SW3. The actual CML cable and reciprocal discovery should identify Gi0/1. Correct only the paper record and preserve the reason; do not move the real cable merely to make it match the old drawing.
sections.heading: Validate a document by preserving disagreements
keyPoints: Mark unknown or unobserved fields explicitly.
Retain the original discrepancy so a later reviewer understands the correction.
sections.explanation: A reliable worksheet records expected and observed cable endpoints, evidence time and resolution status. If observations disagree with the drawing, investigate the physical mapping and both peer configurations before editing the network. Correcting a document may be the right change when the network is already correct.

sections.example: v1.1 2.3 directly covers configuring and verifying both protocols. Announced v2.0 2.3 emphasizes validating documentation with them. This lesson covers both aims but does not prove physical cable category, optical loss, software integrity or user authorization.
sections.heading: Trust and scope remain operational responsibilities
keyPoints: A discovered neighbor is not automatically a trusted device.
Do not publish management addresses or private topology evidence in social captions.
sections.explanation: These discovery advertisements are useful information, not authentication. They can reveal device details to an attached peer. Enable or restrict discovery according to the real edge's requirements; phones and other services may depend on it. Do not recommend globally disabling a protocol without understanding those dependencies.

content.metaTitle: CCNA Day 21: CDP, LLDP and Accurate Topology Records
takeaways: CDP and LLDP describe adjacent advertisements, not complete routing paths.
Keep local and remote device/port fields in their correct direction.
Cross-check reciprocal observations and preserve their timestamps.
Record aging can delay the visible effect of a protocol change.
A missing neighbor advertisement need not mean failed data forwarding.
Discovery information is useful evidence, not authorization or identity proof.
objectives: Configure CDP and LLDP globally and on selected interfaces.
Read local port, remote port, advertised identity and lifetime fields.
Validate both directions of a cable record.
Diagnose an asymmetric LLDP view without assuming the cable failed.
Restore the changed transmit setting and retain honest evidence limitations.
content.plainAnswer: CDP and LLDP describe advertised adjacent neighbors, not the complete routed path or verified ownership. Match each local interface with the neighbor's remote port ID, cross-check from the other end and preserve timestamps. Missing entries can mean disabled transmission, unsupported protocols or expired records as well as a failed link. Confirm data forwarding separately.

firstPractice.hint: A common VLAN permits data forwarding across multiple switches but does not turn a remote switch into a direct neighbor.
firstPractice.task: On paper, interpret a fictional SW2 record: local Gi0/1, system name SW3, remote port Gi0/0. Write the complete cable pair, then state whether this gives SW1 a direct adjacency to SW3.
firstPractice.expected: SW2 Gi0/1 connects to SW3 Gi0/0. SW1 is not directly adjacent to SW3 in this two-cable chain.

beginnerGuide.startingPoint: Draw SW1 Gi0/0 to SW2 Gi0/0, then SW2 Gi0/1 to SW3 Gi0/0. Make separate columns for the interface you are sitting on and the remote port reported by its neighbor.

checkUnderstanding.hint: Separate LLDP advertisement transmission from IP data forwarding.
checkUnderstanding.answer: No. LLDP can be disabled or unsupported while ordinary data forwarding still works. Check protocol settings and record lifetime before replacing a cable or changing VLAN configuration.
checkUnderstanding.question: SW2 loses SW3's LLDP entry but can still ping it. Is that contradictory?

everydayComparison.whereItStops: Advertisements are not verified identity documents. Labels can be stale, absent or misleading, and an advertisement does not test the application's IP path.
everydayComparison.networkMeaning: The local door represents the receiving interface and the reported door represents the remote port ID. Periodic updates resemble discovery advertisements.
everydayComparison.familiarSituation: Two adjacent offices exchange door labels. Each office records its own connecting door and the label reported by the office on the other side, then compares that record with a building plan.

realWorldScenario.title: The drawing is wrong, not the uplink
realWorldScenario.takeaway: Topology documentation is a testable operational claim. Preserve both the discrepancy and its evidence so the correction is auditable rather than merely cosmetic.
realWorldScenario.situation: A hypothetical maintenance worksheet lists a switch uplink on Gi0/2. Current discovery shows the neighbor on Gi0/1, and a reciprocal check agrees. The operator could create an outage by moving a working cable to fit the old drawing. The better first step is to reconcile evidence and change history.

Collect current CDP and LLDP details from both physical cable endpoints.
Compare interface status and the actual cable map, including timestamps and device identity formats.
Resolve whether the network or the document is incorrect before requesting any data-path change.

title: EtherChannel and LACP

lab.goal: Configure both required LACP forms and test one member's failure in each. All expected results are predictions; no author runtime, loss measurement or throughput measurement is claimed. The separate supplemental host procedure A-C and optional T add both-end appliance LACP and a tagged-uplink boundary; they do not claim a tested VM.
setup: Create four fresh entitled CML nodes and the exact four cables. Keep the pairs isolated from one another and from external connectors.

Before configuration, open each node's Console, use enable, then show version and show running-config. Record release and confirm no pre-existing member IPs, channel groups or minimum-links policy; these inspection commands do not modify state.
Preserve the starting lab. Do not use routed configuration on an image that rejects no switchport or Port-channel2 addressing; record unsupported behavior rather than substituting invented output.
Paper alternative: compare configuration roles and predict member states. It does not satisfy the practical Layer 3 branch when no supported runtime is available.

Supplement only: retain all 14 original CML steps. After completing them, use the separate preflight in the first teaching section, then Supplement A, B, C. Only after recovered access service, run optional tagged branch T in the VLAN section; restore it before teardown.

After access recovery, at CSW22 Console enter configure terminal, interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 2, shutdown, end separately. These select and disable the two lab members before the host bond is detached. Keep recovery consoles open.

At APPL22 local Terminal run sudo ip link set bond22 down (disable bond), sudo ip link set enp1s0 down and sudo ip link set enp2s0 down (disable members), then sudo ip link set enp1s0 nomaster and sudo ip link set enp2s0 nomaster (detach). lab.licensingNote: Use an existing Cisco Modeling Labs 2.10 entitlement and its bundled reference images inside CML only. troubleshooting: If passive/passive is configured, neither peer initiates LACP; use the authorized intended active/passive or active/active combination.
If members suspend, compare speed, duplex, access/trunk/native/allowed settings and L2/L3 role on both ends. Preserve diagnostic messages before changing anything.
If the routed branch fails, check that physical members are unaddressed and the /30 belongs to the logical channel. Stop on unsupported virtual features.
If one-member failure drops the whole aggregate, inspect actual remaining participation and any minimum-links policy. Do not force a predicted successful result.

If only one Linux member joins, compare its physical cable/MAC, speed/duplex and partner/aggregator with the other; compare CSW22's flags and partner ports. A successful ping through one link is not a complete two-member baseline.

If Linux changes revert, stop and inspect ownership: this fixture requires empty unmanaged lab NICs. Do not disable a host's global network manager, delete unknown profiles or flush production addresses.

If the bundle is up but data fails, compare access/tag22 and the logical IP placement with PEER22's access22 port. The optional native99 VLAN intentionally carries no test address; it is not a substitute for missing client tag22.

If the whole bundle drops during a one-member fault, inspect actual minimum-links configuration and remaining member eligibility on both ends. Preserve evidence and restore Gi1/0/1; do not force mode on or bypass consistency checks.

glossary.meaning: EtherChannel groups compatible physical links into one logical interface called a port-channel. A member is one physical link in that group; a configured member is not necessarily successfully bundled.

Link Aggregation Control Protocol negotiates compatible aggregation with a peer. Active initiates negotiation; passive responds. Active/active or active/passive can form; passive/passive does not initiate.

A Layer 2 port-channel carries Ethernet VLAN traffic as access or trunk. A Layer 3 port-channel uses no switchport and has an IP address on the logical interface, not separate addresses on its members.
Member attributes must be compatible, including speed, duplex and Layer 2/Layer 3 mode. Layer 2 members must also agree on access VLAN or trunk/native/allowed settings.

A hash selects a member from packet-header fields using a platform's distribution method. Traffic with the same relevant fields commonly stays on one member; one conversation does not automatically use the sum of link speeds.

Bundled means participating in the logical channel. Suspended or standalone states mean the port is not contributing as intended. Read the command's own legend rather than equating every physical up state with a healthy bundle.

A remaining eligible member can preserve logical connectivity after one member fails, subject to configuration such as minimum links. It does not protect against failure of both peer switches or every shared dependency.
Console directly manages a named lab node. The baseline must include member participation, LACP partner evidence and the same traffic test before a controlled member shutdown.

sections.example: Active on SW1 and active on SW2 is deliberate in this lab. A paper alternative changes both peers to passive and predicts no initiated bundle formation. The lab does not make this second fault because the member-shutdown experiment already provides a bounded failure/recovery path.
sections.heading: Negotiation is different from load sharing
keyPoints: Passive does not mean standby-only forwarding.
A peer's channel number can differ; compatibility and partner association matter, not matching labels alone.
sections.explanation:
LACP active initiates while passive responds; at least one side must initiate. Both active and passive members can forward after successful aggregation. PAgP uses different mode names and is not LACP. Static mode on suppresses negotiation and must not be used to hide an unexplained compatibility failure.

Supplement preflight, before sections A-C: APPL22 is an owned x86-64 Ubuntu 24.04 Server appliance fixture with Linux 6.8, iproute2 and ethtool already installed. It has two 1-Gb/s full-duplex NICs with driver speed/duplex reporting. PEER22 is another owned Ubuntu 24.04 Server host with one such NIC. Both have local keyboard/monitor consoles and authorized sudo; no SSH recovery depends on these cables. The fixture has no NetworkManager, DHCP client, bridge, forwarding service or production application on its lab NICs. systemd-networkd must leave these NICs unmanaged. Do not stop global networking to manufacture that condition.

At each host's local Terminal, run uname -r to record its actual kernel, ip -V for iproute2, ip -br address for names/addresses, and ip -d link show for existing masters. Run networkctl status enp1s0 to inspect its setup state; on APPL22 also run networkctl status enp2s0. Require unmanaged lab NICs, no existing addresses/master, and no bond22 or bond22.22. If actual NIC names differ, record their permanent MAC/cable mapping and substitute those names consistently in every command. Stop on ambiguity. Do not flush unknown addresses or replace an existing bond.

At CSW22's direct serial Console, enter enable, show version, show running-config and show vlan brief, each on its own line. These establish authorization, platform/build, configuration and VLAN inventory. Require unused ports 1-3, VLANs22/99 and Port-channel22. Record the baseline; this fixture starts with those three ports shutdown, static access VLAN1, default trunk native1/allowed-all, no channel-group and no extra port policy. Never remove security policy from a shared port to fit this exercise.

sections.example:
The access bundle uses VLAN 10 on both links and an SVI on each switch for testing. A hypothetical member in VLAN 20 is inconsistent, even if its cable is up. A trunk alternative would carry multiple VLANs, but this practical branch intentionally avoids adding trunk variables.

T fault, only after its own successful baseline: at CSW22 Console enter configure terminal, interface Port-channel22, switchport trunk allowed vlan 99, end, separately. This removes tagged client VLAN22 without changing LACP. Read show interfaces trunk and show etherchannel summary; repeat the same two pings and record the data failure with members still bundled. Restore with configure terminal, interface Port-channel22, switchport trunk allowed vlan 22,99, end; verify the allowed list and both original tests. Do not change IPs or force static aggregation to hide the missing VLAN.
sections.heading: Layer 2 members carry one consistent VLAN service
keyPoints: Layer 2 spanning tree treats the channel as a logical link.
A successful ping through one member can hide failure of the other.
sections.explanation:
An access bundle needs the same access VLAN on its members. A trunk bundle needs compatible trunk encapsulation, native VLAN and allowed lists. Speed and duplex must also be compatible. Once grouped, make intended service changes consistently through the logical interface according to platform behavior and verify all members.

Optional tagged-uplink branch T runs only AFTER the access baseline and member-fault recovery in A-C. A network appliance may use one untagged data network; a virtualized host may carry several tagged guest networks. LACP does not choose the VLAN policy. This exercise tests a Linux VLAN subinterface over the same bond, not a VM or a hypervisor product's licensing/features. A real hypervisor also needs matching guest-port/virtual-switch settings and guest tests; those remain supporting coverage only.

At CSW22's direct Console (#), enter configure terminal (global mode), vlan 99 (create the unused native VLAN), exit (global mode), interface Port-channel22 (select the logical bundle), switchport mode trunk (fixed tagged service), switchport trunk native vlan 99 (untagged boundary), switchport trunk allowed vlan 22,99 (only these VLANs), switchport nonegotiate (no dynamic trunk negotiation), then end (EXEC). Enter each command separately. Read show interfaces trunk and each member's show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/1 switchport and show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/2 switchport; require matching inherited settings before continuing.

At APPL22's local Terminal, enter sudo ip address del 192.0.2.22/24 dev bond22 (remove only the lab address from the untagged parent), sudo ip link add link bond22 name bond22.22 type vlan id 22 (create the tag-22 attachment), sudo ip address add 192.0.2.22/24 dev bond22.22 (place the address there), then sudo ip link set bond22.22 up (enable it), separately. The members stay unaddressed; native99 has no test IP. PEER22 remains an untagged access22 host. Read ip -d link show bond22.22 for VLAN id22 and ip -br address for address placement; test ping -I bond22.22 -c 4 192.0.2.23 and PEER22's reverse ping.

sections.example: RSW1's Port-channel2 is 203.0.113.1/30 and RSW2's is .2/30. Their Gi0/0 and Gi0/1 members have no IP addresses. This is an adjacent routed-link test; no static routing or transit service is configured between the two separate lab pairs.
sections.heading: Layer 3 addressing belongs to the aggregate
keyPoints: Use fresh nodes rather than converting the working Layer 2 pair mid-experiment.
If routed channel support is absent, stop this branch and label it unperformed.
sections.explanation:
For the routed design, create Port-channel2 as a Layer 3 interface, assign its /30 address, and join compatible unaddressed routed members. Do not put one subnet address on each member or retain access/trunk membership. The two ends use distinct addresses in the same directly connected subnet.

The host supplement is still a Layer 2 switch port-channel even though the Linux bond owns an IP address. CSW22 carries access VLAN22; it does not route and has no SVI in this rack. APPL22 is the IP endpoint at 192.0.2.22/24, and PEER22 is 192.0.2.23/24 on the same VLAN. No default route, DNS, NAT or Internet path is needed. The original RSW1/RSW2 example remains the separate routed-channel exercise.

The host track requires one real switch LACP system at both cable ends. Do not connect the two NICs to independent switches and assume that matching channel numbers creates a multichassis peer. No stacking, multichassis feature, hypervisor entitlement, virtual appliance image or Cisco image export is implied. If this owned equipment or supported Linux driver is absent, do a paper configuration/partner-state prediction and label the practical branch unperformed.

sections.example: Two member counters need not rise equally for one ping stream. A single stream can consistently select one link. Do not alter global load-balancing policy simply to make counters equal, and do not interpret a virtual interface's displayed speed as measured capacity.
sections.heading: Read participation and distribution separately
keyPoints: A suspended or standalone member needs investigation even if the logical peer responds.
CML's virtual performance limits make this a configuration exercise, not a bandwidth benchmark.
sections.explanation:
show etherchannel summary includes a legend for logical type, use and member participation. On common IOS output S denotes Layer 2, R Layer 3, U in use and P a bundled member, but read the displayed legend rather than guessing. show lacp neighbor identifies partner negotiation. Distribution uses platform-selected header fields and may be uneven.

Host-track interpretation: a Linux bond can exist while neither intended member has completed negotiation. Require the active aggregator to contain both named NICs with the same partner system, not merely two carrier-up entries. On CSW22 the partner system identifies APPL22's bond; on APPL22 the partner identifies CSW22. These are opposite endpoints, so the two displayed partner MACs should not be required to equal each other.

A two-port healthy baseline followed by a one-port fault and two-port recovery demonstrates only this lab's redundancy behavior. Record actual convergence and any missed replies. The 100-ms link-check interval is not a 100-ms end-to-end recovery guarantee. Fast LACP requests short control-packet timing; it does not promise zero loss or double a single transfer's throughput. The exact Linux source documentation is linked in section B and bound to supplemental coverage pointers.

sections.example:
This lab shuts one already-bundled member on each independent pair, then retests through the remaining member. No minimum-links requirement is configured. An unexpected total failure should be investigated, not reported as a successful failover. Recovery requires both restored participation and the original peer result.

After host teardown, at CSW22 Console (#), type each cleanup command separately: configure terminal enters global mode; interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 2 selects the two disabled former members; no channel-group detaches them; exit returns to global; no interface Port-channel22 deletes the lab aggregate; interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 3 selects the three lab ports; shutdown restores idle state; switchport access vlan 1 restores the prepared access baseline; end returns to EXEC. Read show vlan brief and show running-config. Only when no remaining attachment uses the exercise VLANs, enter configure terminal, no vlan 22, no vlan 99, end: remove the lab-created VLANs, omitting 99 if T was not run. VLAN database changes can persist without a startup-config save.
sections.heading: Recover a member without forcing a loop
keyPoints: No zero-loss or exact convergence-time guarantee is made.
v1.1 2.4 and v2.0 2.1.c include both Layer 2 and Layer 3 LACP, so both practical branches are explicit.
sections.explanation:
Compare peer cabling, speed/duplex, Layer 2/Layer 3 role, VLAN attributes and negotiation modes when bundling fails. Preserve relevant error output. Correct the proven mismatch under an approved plan; do not force on mode, disable spanning tree or remove a live member from aggregation without considering loops.

Supplement rollback T: first restore allowed VLANs22,99 and prove the tagged baseline again. Then, at APPL22's local Terminal, run sudo ip link delete bond22.22 to remove only the disposable VLAN interface and its address, followed by sudo ip address add 192.0.2.22/24 dev bond22 to restore the untagged attachment. At CSW22's direct Console enter configure terminal, interface Port-channel22, no switchport nonegotiate, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 22, switchport trunk native vlan 1, switchport trunk allowed vlan all, end, one at a time. These restore the access service and baseline dormant trunk attributes; all is not an active trunk after the mode is access. Read the logical and both physical switchport settings, then rerun section C's two-member and bidirectional access tests. If rejected or inconsistent, stop traffic and restore the captured dedicated-port configuration rather than splitting a live bundle.

Teardown is separate from fault recovery. Restore and verify the working access baseline before the cleanup list. Shut the switch's two members before detaching the host bond, so two formerly aggregated cables cannot become unintended independent paths. Remove only exercise-owned interfaces/addresses/VLANs. Do not unload the bonding driver, stop systemd-networkd, erase switch configuration or alter other lab pairs.

sections.example: At CSW22 Console (#), enter configure terminal (global mode), interface GigabitEthernet1/0/3 (PEER22's single cable), switchport mode access (untagged service), switchport access vlan 22 (same data VLAN), no shutdown (enable the prepared peer port), end (EXEC). PEER22 does not join a port-channel. Port-channel22 is local naming, not a VLAN identifier negotiated with Linux: the shared service uses VLAN22 because we explicitly configured it. Continue to section B before enabling the two appliance members.
sections.heading: Supplement A: connect an owned appliance to one switch
keyPoints: This is a physical Layer 2 host attachment, separate from both original CML switch pairs. No practical evidence is borrowed between tracks.
Use existing lawful switch firmware and Linux software. Do not obtain or export Cisco virtual images for this rack.
A prepared appliance representative tests networking, not a monitoring/firewall product or production application.
The stated hardware/software is a reproducible conditional fixture, not a claim that it was available or executed by the author.
sections.explanation:
Use a separate isolated rack: CSW22 is an owned WS-C2960X-24TS-L with LAN Base, IOS 15.2(7)E, and direct serial/USB Console at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control. APPL22 enp1s0 connects to CSW22 Gi1/0/1; enp2s0 to Gi1/0/2. PEER22 enp1s0 connects to Gi1/0/3. These are the only three cables. No uplink, Wi-Fi, bridge to a host network, NAT connector or connection to the original CML pairs is allowed. All nodes have their own supplies; PoE is not an appliance requirement here.

After the supplement preflight, at CSW22's direct Console (#), enter each command separately: configure terminal enters global mode; vlan 22 creates the data VLAN; exit returns to global mode; interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 2 selects exactly the two appliance cables; shutdown keeps them down during construction; switchport mode access sets untagged service; switchport access vlan 22 selects that broadcast domain; channel-group 22 mode active places them in Po22 and initiates LACP; end returns to EXEC. Leave the two members shutdown until section B is complete. Never substitute mode on.

At the same CSW22 Console, enter configure terminal, then interface Port-channel22, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 22, no shutdown, end, each on its own line. These enter global mode, select the logical interface, explicitly confirm access/VLAN22 service, enable the logical interface and return to EXEC. Do not configure a minimum-links requirement of two: this experiment deliberately tests operation with one member. Require no existing min-links setting in the captured fresh Po22 configuration.

sections.example: Read the Linux 6.8 bonding documentation at https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.8/networking/bonding.html for mode, monitoring and partner behavior. The primary iproute2 bond-option parser and ip-link/ip-address manuals are recorded in supplement coverage. At APPL22's local Terminal, ethtool enp1s0 and ethtool enp2s0 read speed/duplex/link detection after the switch enables the links. Require both 1000 Mb/s, full duplex and compatible driver reporting; stop on a mismatch instead of forcing unknown settings. The interface names are the preflight's recorded cable mapping, not universal Linux names.
sections.heading: Supplement B: create and address the Linux LACP peer
keyPoints: sudo authorizes each named local change; it is not permission to reconfigure an unrelated management NIC.
An unmanaged fixture prevents a network manager from silently replacing this temporary configuration. Do not add conflicting Netplan files during this exercise.
The host uses LACP mode 802.3ad, not active-backup. Two physical cables alone do not establish a negotiated aggregate.
If the kernel/driver rejects the bond or required option, capture the error and mark the branch unsupported. A paper answer is not host runtime evidence.
sections.explanation:
At APPL22's local keyboard/monitor Terminal, run commands separately; stop on errors. sudo modprobe bonding max_bonds=0 loads the driver without an automatic bond0; an already-loaded driver keeps its settings. sudo ip link set enp1s0 down and sudo ip link set enp2s0 down hold the verified empty NICs down. sudo ip link add bond22 type bond mode 802.3ad miimon 100 lacp_rate fast min_links 1 creates the bond: 802.3ad selects LACP, miimon 100 checks carrier every 100 ms, lacp_rate fast requests short partner control timing, and min_links 1 permits one usable member. It neither persists across reboot nor measures recovery.

At APPL22's local Terminal, run sudo ip link set enp1s0 master bond22, then sudo ip link set enp2s0 master bond22. Each attaches only the named NIC. Run sudo ip address add 192.0.2.22/24 dev bond22 to address the logical endpoint, not its members. Run sudo ip link set bond22 up, sudo ip link set enp1s0 up and sudo ip link set enp2s0 up separately to enable the logical and physical interfaces. Run ip -br address to confirm address ownership and ip -d link show bond22 to read actual mode/options. Do not add a gateway.

At PEER22's local Terminal, run sudo ip address add 192.0.2.23/24 dev enp1s0 to add its only lab IP, then sudo ip link set enp1s0 up to enable that single link. Run ip -br address to check it. This peer is not bonded. Both hosts must already permit the isolated ICMP test under their existing policy; do not disable firewalls to force replies.

At CSW22's direct Console (#), enter configure terminal, interface range GigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 2, no shutdown, end, one per line. These enter global mode, select the completed appliance members, enable them and return to EXEC. Keep all three local consoles open. Allow actual LACP negotiation and spanning-tree forwarding before judging traffic.

sections.example: Evidence table to fill yourself: baseline has intended member count 2; single-member fault has intended count 1; restored state has intended count 2. For each row record CSW22 flags/partners, Linux active aggregator and member state, both actual ping results and time observed. A ping that works with only one member at the starting baseline is insufficient: it cannot validate the intended two-link build. This is a learner procedure with expected states, not an author-generated capture.
sections.heading: Supplement C: verify both peers, fail one member, recover
keyPoints: A host's partner is the switch and the switch's partner is the host; compare each against the intended other endpoint.
Do not move the logical IP onto a surviving NIC. Both members serve the same logical host attachment.
The test covers one cable/member outage, not switch failure, appliance failure or application availability.
Branch T has its own tagged baseline and missing-VLAN fault. An LACP success does not prove that VLAN22 is allowed.
sections.explanation:
Baseline at CSW22's direct Console (#): show etherchannel summary reads logical use and member flags; show lacp neighbor reads the actual partner on each cable; show interfaces Port-channel22 switchport confirms access VLAN22; show mac address-table interface Port-channel22 locates the host MAC after traffic. Run each separately. Require Layer 2 Po22 in use and both Gi1/0/1 and Gi1/0/2 bundled according to the displayed legend. The two partner entries must identify the same APPL22 system with distinct partner ports.

Baseline at APPL22's local Terminal: cat /proc/net/bonding/bond22 reads mode, active aggregator, member status and partner details. Require IEEE 802.3ad mode, two members in the active aggregator, both named NICs link-up with the same aggregator/CSW22 partner, and no unexplained churn. Read actual output; do not copy a predicted transcript. ping -I bond22 -c 4 192.0.2.23 sends four requests through the bond. At PEER22's local Terminal, ping -I enp1s0 -c 4 192.0.2.22 tests the reverse direction. Require both tests before faulting.

Fault at CSW22's direct Console (#): enter configure terminal (global), interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1 (only the first member), shutdown (disable it), end (EXEC). Leave Gi1/0/2, Po22 and PEER22 enabled. Repeat both switch show commands, APPL22's /proc read and both identical pings while the fault remains. Expect one participating link after convergence, with the original IP on bond22 and service possible through Gi1/0/2. Record actual lost replies; no timing or zero-loss promise is made.

Recover at CSW22's direct Console (#): enter configure terminal, interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1, no shutdown, end, separately. These select and re-enable the same failed member. Repeat every baseline readback and both pings. Require two negotiated members again, not just link lights. Only then attempt optional branch T or use the cleanup list to remove this disposable rack configuration.

content.metaTitle: CCNA Day 22: Layer 2 and Layer 3 LACP EtherChannel
takeaways: LACP negotiation requires at least one active initiator.
Member compatibility matters more than the local channel number.
Layer 2 carries VLANs; Layer 3 puts addressing on the aggregate.
Verify every intended member, not just logical ping success.
A single flow does not automatically consume summed member bandwidth.
Restore a failed member and verify negotiation before claiming full recovery.
A host/appliance LACP peer needs its own configuration and partner/member evidence; a second switch is not a substitute.
VLAN tagging and link aggregation are independent choices. A healthy bundle can still carry the wrong or missing VLAN.
objectives: Predict active/active, active/passive and passive/passive negotiation.
Configure both access and routed LACP channels.
Verify partner identity and member bundling instead of relying on link-up state.
Diagnose consistency problems without forcing static aggregation.
Test and restore one member in each isolated channel type.
Configure an owned dual-NIC Linux appliance and its switch LACP peer, verify both ends, then test and undo a single-link fault.
content.plainAnswer: LACP combines compatible links into a logical port-channel when at least one side initiates negotiation. A Layer 2 channel carries VLAN traffic; a Layer 3 channel has its IP address on the logical interface with unaddressed routed members. Verify both partner negotiation and member participation. Redundancy can preserve service after one link fails, but one flow does not automatically gain all members' combined bandwidth.

everydayComparison.whereItStops: EtherChannel uses header-based selection, not a human queue manager. The analogy does not predict exact bandwidth, perfect fairness or packet timing.
everydayComparison.networkMeaning: The shared queue resembles a logical port-channel and the lanes resemble members. A selection method distributes different traffic across available members.
everydayComparison.familiarSituation: Several compatible checkout lanes serve one queue, but one purchase is assigned to a lane rather than split item-by-item across every cashier.

prerequisites: Understand access VLANs, SVIs and routed physical ports.
Use four fresh IOSvL2 nodes under an existing CML 2.10 entitlement.
Check actual image support for LACP and routed port-channels before any experiment.
